Dear all,

I've opened my second PR to mathlib: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/37814. It proves an equivalence of categories between two models for the category of Hopf algebras over a commutative ring. There ended up being more to do than I was expecting, so I apologize for the length (and for any stylistic crimes committed).

Looking forward to any feedback!

Thanks,

Saul

@Robin Carlier explained on this PR that there are currently some bad defects in Mathlib preventing this being done nicely --- I think they say that the root cause is that we are relying on defeqs for the constructions of the tensor product in ModuleCat too much?

Does anyone have ideas about where to go from here? It would be lovely to get this result in...

The root cause is also explained in #mathlib4 > Diamond in category theory : the issue is not only the tensor product of ModuleCat, but overall the design of the existing equivalence between AlgCat R and Mon (ModuleCat R) which creates bad diamonds, that are just further amplified here. I am also not sure what the right way forward is, but we should think about and fix the design of this equivalence first before building more equivalences of this kind.

I think one possible way is to simply give up the defeq: we should perhaps be proving that a certain functor from AlgCat to Mon (ModuleCat) (which is the direction that forgets the problematic zpow field that is missing in the target) is an equivalence (rather than constructing an actual inverse that creates bad instances). This is essentially making the objects of the inverse as a type alias, and the cost is that we have to perhaps constantly transport things through the unit/counit isomorphisms of the equivalence.
I have not thought that much about it, so perhaps this is not a good way.
